correctness.rationale: Fix a finite join A and standard k. The relation that the e-th A^(k)-oracle computation outputs 1 on y is arithmetical in A. If all model sets were Turing reducible to A^(k), each would have a total characteristic index and the resulting arithmetical formula would uniformly enumerate the whole second-order part. Pakhomov's Theorem 6.1 states that Sigma1_1-Rfn refutes uniform enumeration by every arithmetical formula, including with set parameters. Hence some model set escapes the bound. The proof does not conflate per-k escape with one set escaping all k.

value.rationale: Omega-models in reverse mathematics are naturally studied via their Turing ideals. Turning the source's formula-enumeration obstruction into the statement that every fixed finite jump cone over finitely many internal parameters misses an internal set yields a concrete, reusable model invariant. It rules out principal and fixed-jump-bounded ideals and clarifies what computational richness reflection forces without asserting jump closure.
